title: Claudot: AI Agents inside your Godot 🥐
author: unwittingyeti
selftext:
Hello makers and gamers,

Godot is an amazing tool for making games. I love how small it is and that I can even run it on my old laptop... there's only one problem.

How the heck do I alt tab on Ubuntu??

I've googled it and I still can't remember between sessions so instead I built CLAUDOT so that I could have Claude inside my Godot! Over the last six months Claudot has grown, learned, evolved and matured.

One built-in feature I like is the forced-context-injector which, when checked, forces the most recent documentation for classes, functions and methods you use into the prompt itself. Similar to the old Context7 MCP but specifically focused on GDscript.

If you'd like to check it out you can find more info over at [https://claudotcode.com/](https://claudotcode.com/)

comments.author: BetaTester704
comments.body:
Novel at best.

You will never get a good maintainable project using it.

replies.author: unwittingyeti
replies.body:
Thank you for taking the time to actually respond with an argument. Genuinely appreciated.

I think you're pretty much right on about the maintainable part... but I'm just not sure what it means. I can see a future of gaming where games are a bit more 'disposable' than they are today. More like a movie where you pay a few bucks to have fun for a night with friends, as opposed to paying medium bucks to own a game you might play for 100s of hours. I think there might be room for both types.

All I know after using these tools for a year is that a tsunami is coming and when it gets here in earnest I want to be handing out shovels!

comments.author: unwittingyeti
comments.body:
To anyone showing up to my almost week-old post with only an emoji, gross gif or elementary school insult line:

Thank you for the engagement!

But also I would challenge you to use your words. Put together an argument. Tell me why you hate it and what you hate about it. I want to have that discussion.

I'm not sure I like the AI. I was in the games industry for a bunch of years on the publishing and rarely, but joyously on design teams, and was laid off the moment chatGPT came out. I understand the threat the industry faces. I understand that these tools were created on the pilfered knowledge of all humanity and especially the gamemakers who came before me, and I don't like that one bit.

But I also acknowledge that these are the most uniquely powerful tools I have ever used and there is no way that I can see that the future of game making does not include these tools. I spent my years in the professional games industry wishing I had jumped in sooner. I'm not finna make that mistake again.

If anybody has an argument, anecdote, perspective or even just a coherent thought I would be happy to read it.
